correctness.rationale: Use basis idempotents, U, V and W=U⊗V; unit form d1,d2,d3,x,y,z. Coadjoint fixing is equivalent to vanishing of f([g,h]) on all basis h, giving α(x)=β(y)=−C(z), C(−,y)=(d1−d2)α, C(x,−)=−(d2−d3)β, (d1−d3)C=0. At C=0, count 0/1/2 nonzero arrow functionals and free idempotent-dual coefficients. For rank-s nonzero C, d1=d3, with free h=d1−d2 if and only if both α and β lie in the two images of C; otherwise h=0. The rank-s radicals determine stabilizer dimensions and orbit sizes q^(2s+1)(q−1) or q^(2s+2)(q−1)^2. Multiplying by the Gaussian-binomial rank-s matrix count and dividing by orbit sizes proves all table entries; weighted mass totals q^(3+a+b+ab). Fresh independent exact q-ary mass checks and direct actual upper-triangular stabilizers for a=b=1, q=2,3 corroborate.
